@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+# Checkpoint ladder, rung 2 — two acts, one join. Decided in advance (2026-09-06);
+# NOTHING here is authored by hand downstream: Aristotle formalizes the Law from the
+# three approved values, Aristotle authors the recipe from the intent, an unnamed
+# agent executes it, and the Law fires on the terminal state. See ../README.md.
+#
+# What this rung proves over rung 1: a recipe with TWO governed acts, the second
+# depending on the first's effect (the receipt names the item the declaration
+# minted), so the run needs a readiness receipt per act; and a Law that grounds
+# on TWO relations joined on a key. The kernel already refuses a lot-tracked
+# receipt without a lot (apotheke INV-7), so the Law asks for what the kernel does
+# NOT enforce: the supplier's own lot reference on every received lot.
+#
+# Live baseline (apotheke.sokrates.is, 2026-09-06 15:00Z): one warehouse
+# ("Krates warehouse"), one supplier ("Nordtæki Dreifing ehf."), nine items all
+# lot-tracked, seven lots all carrying a supplier_lot_ref — so a correct run
+# leaves the set empty and rung 3's defect (omit the reference) yields one row.
+
+terminal_law_name: received_lot_without_supplier_ref
+goal_statement: >-
+  Every lot received into the apotheke inventory record for a lot-tracked item
+  carries the supplier's own lot reference.
+definition_of_done: >-
+  The work is complete when every lot in the apotheke lot projection whose item is
+  lot-tracked in the apotheke item projection carries a supplier lot reference. A
+  lot of a lot-tracked item whose supplier lot reference is absent is a violation,
+  and the violation names the lot by its lot_id and its item by item_id. When the
+  condition holds the violation set is empty.
+
+# The operator intent Aristotle authors the recipe from
+# (polis-ergon author-hypernode --intent ... --terminal-law-name received_lot_without_supplier_ref).
+recipe_intent: >-
+  Declare one inventory item and receive its first delivery into the apotheke
+  inventory record, as two governed acts in order. First, one apotheke append
+  carrying exactly one item_declared event for the item the kickoff names (name,
+  base unit, scale, optional sku and tags), tracking lot, effective from today, a
+  fresh item id, and an idempotency key derived from the kickoff. Second, once the
+  declared item can be read back from the apotheke item projection, one apotheke
+  append carrying exactly one goods_received event for that item: the quantity the
+  kickoff gives, into the location and from the supplier counterparty the kickoff
+  names (their ids resolved by reading the apotheke location and counterparty
+  projections, never invented), cause purchase, the unit cost and currency the
+  kickoff gives with the extended cost as their product, occurred now, a fresh
+  movement id, and a new lot with a fresh lot id carrying the supplier lot
+  reference the kickoff gives; idempotency key derived from the kickoff so a retry
+  never receives the delivery twice. Appends nothing else. Completion is attested
+  from the record: read the new lot back from the apotheke lot projection and
+  confirm it belongs to the declared item and carries the supplier lot reference.
+
+# The kickoff handed to the run (polis-ergon dispatch --kickoff ...).
+kickoff: >-
+  Declare the item "Thermal pad, 40 mm square": base unit "unit", scale 0, sku
+  "TG-40", tags ["consumable", "workshop"]. Then receive 12 units of it into the
+  location "Krates warehouse" from the supplier "Nordtæki Dreifing ehf." at a unit
+  cost of 1250 ISK, supplier lot reference "ND-TG-2026-09", no expiry.
+
+# The benchmark shape — what a correct pass looks like, checked against the artifacts
+# Aristotle produces and the run's verification, never against exact text.
+expected:
+  law:
+    relations: [apotheke_lot_projection, apotheke_item_projection]  # joined on item_id
+    predicates: 2                           # item is lot-tracked; the reference is absent
+    absence_shaped: false                   # a missing column value, not a negated subquery
+  recipe:
+    erga: [apotheke/append_events, apotheke/append_events]  # declare, then receive

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Model two calls without duplicating the erga ref**

When this pair is graded against an Aristotle-authored recipe, this expectation is impossible: `Recipe._unique_erga` in `aristotle/src/aristotle/recipe.py` rejects duplicate refs because `erga` is the unique tool basis, while runtime attention may invoke `apotheke/append_events` twice. Repeating the ref therefore makes authoring retry or fail, but emitting the valid single ref fails this corpus assertion, so rung 2 can never pass; keep the ref once and grade the two executed acts from the run receipts or completed calls instead.
